summary: The main hypothesis was confirmed: a branch-and-bound solver with coloring bounds, augmented by a Dynamic Local Search (DLS) tabu fallback for hard dense instances, achieved a perfect score of 100 out of 100 on the Maximum Clique problem. The greedy-only control scored 33.76, confirming that naive approaches are far insufficient.
key_points: h-main (BnB + DLS hybrid) scored 100 vs. predicted ≥90 — CONFIRMED. The solver finds optimal cliques across all test cases within the 2-second time limit.
h-control-negative (greedy by degree) scored 33.76 vs. predicted <50 — CONFIRMED. This validates that exhaustive or sophisticated search is essential for maximum clique.
Key insight: pure BnB with greedy coloring bound alone reaches ~88–90 on the hardest dense graphs; the DLS tabu search fallback is critical for closing the remaining gap to 100 on those cases.
No further iteration is needed — the solution already achieves the maximum possible score of 100.
